schedule_str: predicted report date from each firm's own past report calendar, known at the prior close
execution_str: decision at prior close, entry and exit at the open; central cost 10 bps each way
grade_reason: 0 of 47 frozen tests and no reference book clear the bar. Closest test, the 9 sessions ending 2 sessions before the predicted report: +0.19% on Russell 1000 (t 3.4, BH q 0.028, alpha t 3.0) against a 0.20% round trip and a 0.30% size bar; the S&P 500 partner fails (+0.10%, alpha t 1.6); per trade it is +0.06% (t 1.9); the announcement premium is absent in large caps (-0.04%). The off-season +0.35% (t 3.4) cut was read after the results: a forward-log lead only.
new_family_proposal: earnings_announcement_events: Price effects tied to each firm's own scheduled earnings report: the announcement-month premium (Frazzini-Lamont, Savor-Wilson), a firm's own history of report reactions, early/late report timing and post-announcement drift. Why it should pay is compensation for bearing announcement-information risk and attention-driven demand, plus slow reaction to the news; the trigger is a firm-specific event date, not a market-wide calendar flow (month end, rebalances, expiries) and not a price-momentum rank. No current family covers it: calendar_and_flow is flows on shared calendar dates; equity_cross_sectional_momentum ranks on past returns; index_and_listing_events is index and listing milestones. This is not an escape from a big count: calendar_and_flow is the SMALLER family here, and moving 964 trials out of it lowers its N (the DSR N of the live month-end pods). Fallback if the family is refused: calendar_and_flow for the whole 1,254 (the conservative choice for those pods).

mechanism_str: Trend continuation after a base: a stock moving above a rising 30-week average out of a flat base is under-priced slow-diffusion information; stage 4 (declining) names keep underperforming.
expected_sign_and_location_str: Stage 2 leads (positive forward return), stage 4 lags; book Sharpe above exposure-matched SPXTR; edge not explained by momentum.
universe_str: PIT Russell 1000 (primary), Russell 3000, S&P 500; 25 ETFs and BTC (GBTC proxy); 1992-2026
schedule_str: weekly bar; stage map from 30/40-week averages and slope; 10-week-mean exit chosen as S1
execution_str: next-open fills, 10 bps/side, T-bill cash; two cost layers
grade_reason: Rejected as a mechanical strategy: the literal weekly stage-2 base-breakout book on PIT R1000 1992-2026 is 13.6%/yr, Sharpe 0.72, max DD -39% vs SPXTR 0.53. It beats the exposure-matched index in validation (P 0.99) but fails confirmation (P 0.17; 7.6%/yr vs 15.5%); S1 fails confirmation. Only stage 4 underperformance passes the frozen cell rule (-1.26% in 13 weeks in all eras); stage 2 has no edge (+0.03%) and is explained by momentum and volatility.
overlap_note: Re-evaluates stock breakout-style books like radge_trend_blueprint_study (this batch) and the Radge WTT rows; no evaluation is re-run exactly. Cites radge_trend_blueprint_study as a source.
notes: Family: stage 2 = base breakout above a rising moving average with trailing exits = trend / breakout, same as the Radge stock breakouts; 'stage 2 is explained by momentum' is a result, not the mechanism studied. Trials: book_random_rank (20 random-rank books; E0001 = 22 books + 2 cost layers + 2 universes + 20 random ranks + 3 controls = 49) is a null and is subtracted: 182 - 20 = 162. Assets (26: 25 ETFs and BTC) and the 3 breadth gates sit in the same family and are kept.
